brief: The S&P 500 has fallen 12% from its October 6 high, more than the median 10% peak-to-trough decline since 1980; forward P/E has dropped 25% YTD to 16x, close to its historical average, but the multiple on trend EPS ranks in the 83rd percentile since 1990 because the AI investment boom has lifted earnings about 25% above their 30-year trend, creating downside risk as capex tailwinds fade. Applying the 30-year average multiple of 17x to trend EPS of $340 implies a downside level near 5,800; if confidence in the consensus earnings forecast returns and the multiple recovers to the 10-year average, the index would reach a new high of 8,100. This week the sell-off broadened from an AI-specific unwind into a wider growth shock: cyclicals, which had tracked defensives for most of the past month, lagged by 5pp over the past ten days. Goldman recommends diversifying into defensives and buyback-heavy names and is watching for one of three catalysts to mark a bottom: renewed confidence in AI earnings, a dovish Fed signal, or a major decline in investor positioning. Positioning has not cleared: hedge fund leverage is at its lowest since April 2025, but $170bn of fund inflows since Q4 and futures length in the 82nd percentile keep sentiment elevated.
